StrategicRisk Partners | Capabilities

What can we help you evaluate?

Start with the decision you need to make. We agree on the records we can use, the question the analysis will answer and the deliverable before work begins. Software engagements begin with a scoped prototype.

Illustrative case | Comparing fuel offers during engine downtime

Suppose a seven-day engine delay requires replacement lift at $5,000 per day and 10,000 gallons of fuel. The original budget allowed $4.00 per gallon. Supplier A can deliver all the fuel at $4.60 per gallon. Supplier B offers $4.25 per gallon plus a $2,000 fee.

The replacement aircraft adds $35,000. Including fuel above budget, A adds $41,000 in total and B adds $39,500. B saves $1,500 after its fee. A third supplier offering only 7,000 gallons leaves a 3,000-gallon gap to cover before its price can be compared.

Hypothetical inputs for illustration. The replacement rate excludes fuel.

Industry classifications

Primary NAICS: 541690 — Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services. Additional classifications:

541511 · Custom Computer Programming541512 · Computer Systems Design541611 · Management Consulting541715 · Physical and Engineering R&D

NAICS 541715 includes industry-specific size-standard exceptions relating to aircraft and aircraft engines, other aircraft components, and guided missiles and space vehicles. Listing an industry classification does not represent a government certification, contract award, engineering authorization, or demonstrated past performance.

Fuel procurement & disruption cash exposure

Change fictional procurement assumptions to see how unit price, delivery fees and replacement-lift days affect incremental cash requirements. This is a transparent what-if calculator—not live fuel pricing or an operational hedge.

Concept demonstration | Input-driven

Change the assumptions

Incremental cash exposure over budget

Supplier A | extra cost$41,000
Supplier B | extra cost$39,500

Lower modeled incremental cost

Supplier B

B is $1,500 below A with these assumptions.

Method: incremental cost = replacement-lift days × daily rate + gallons × (offer price − budget price) + applicable delivery fee. Negative values mean below the budget comparator, not guaranteed savings. This assumes each supplier covers the full fuel requirement.

Starting values match the worked example elsewhere on this site. Rates are made up for explanation, not fetched from commodity markets.

Assessment boundary

SentinelGate is an internal prototype, not a production SIEM, independent third-party audit, CMMC assessment or certified Zero Trust platform. Evidence integrity does not mean a control is MET.
